text: Unified LLM effects. The doeff-llm package defines the effects of talking to a language model once, for every provider.
LLM Chat, LLM Streaming Chat, LLM Structured Query and LLM Embedding name what the program asks for.
The provider packages, OpenAI, Gemini and OpenRouter, bring only handlers that answer them.
Before doeff-llm, each provider package defined its own, near-identical effects.
Those names remain as deprecated aliases: subclasses of LLM Chat that warn when they are built.
Now one program yields the same LLM Chat. Only the model name says which provider should answer.
Under the same handlers, OpenAI answers gpt-4o, and Gemini answers gemini 1.5 pro.
Here is the page's example: one workflow, three models, and three provider handlers in one stack. Mock handlers stand in for the real ones, so no API is called.
Each handler reads effect dot model. The structured query for gpt-4o reaches OpenAI first, which supports it, and answers.
The chat for gemini 1.5 pro is not OpenAI's. The handler yields Pass, with k, and the next handler out, Gemini, answers.
Mistral large passes OpenAI and Gemini, and reaches OpenRouter, the catch-all on the outside.
A handler's annotation filters effects too. chat only is annotated effect colon LLM Chat.
The structured query does not match, so it skips chat only without a call, and any model answers it.
The LLM Chat matches. chat only is called, and answers it.
So the order of the stack matters. OpenRouter answers a chat for any model.
Install it innermost, and it answers all three effects. OpenAI and Gemini never see one.
The catch-all goes outermost, and every handler inside it passes on the models it does not support.
One effect says what the program asks for. The handlers decide who answers, by handling it, or passing it on with k.
